q-132168.name: Question 1
q-132168.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{3}),$ calculate $P(X\le 2).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
q-132168.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{3}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x/3}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(X\le 2)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{{e}^{-x/3}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-2/3}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.4866\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

q-253927.name: Question 16
q-253927.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{2}{5}),$ calculate $P(X>7\,|\,X>2).$
q-253927.worked_solution:
Given a random variable $X∼Exp(\lambda ),$ and two positive real numbers $s,t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =\frac{2}{5},$ $s=2,$ and $s+t=7.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=7-2=5
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>7\,|\,X>2) & ={e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & ={e}^{-(2/5)\cdot (5)} \\  & ={e}^{-2} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the random variable X∼Exp(25), calculate P(X>7|X>2).

a
 1e2
b
 12e4
c
 1e6
d
 13e8
e
 1e7
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a random variable X∼Exp(λ), and two positive real numbers s,t, the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that P(X>s+t|X>s)=P(X>t)=e−λt.

In our case, we have λ=25, s=2, and s+t=7. From this, we can find t as follows: t=(t+s)−s=7−2=5

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get P(X>7|X>2)=e−λt=e−(2/5)⋅(5)=e−2=1e2.

q-253887.name: Question 17
q-253887.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{2}),$ calculate $P(X>3\,|\,X>1).$
q-253887.worked_solution:
Given a random variable $X∼Exp(\lambda ),$ and two positive real numbers $s,t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =2,$ $s=1,$ and $s+t=3.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=3-1=2
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>3\,|\,X>1) & ={e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & ={e}^{-(1/2)\cdot (2)} \\  & ={e}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-253932.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(5),$ calculate $P(X\le 6\,|\,X>4).$
q-253932.worked_solution:

$$

$$
P(X\le s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-{e}^{-\lambda t}
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =5,$ $s=4,$ and $s+t=6.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=6-4=2
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 6\,|\,X>4) & =1-{e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & =1-{e}^{-(5)\cdot (2)} \\  & =1-{e}^{-10}\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the random variable X∼Exp(3), calculate P(X≤13|X>14).

a
e−1/6
b
e−1/4
c
1−e−1/6
d
1−e−1/24
e
1−e−1/4

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Given a random variable X∼Exp(λ), and two positive real numbers s,t, the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that P(X>s+t|X>s)=P(X>t)=e−λt.

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows: P(X≤s+t|X>s)=1−P(X>s+t|X>s)=1−e−λt

In our case, we have λ=3, s=14, and s+t=13. From this, we can find t as follows: t=(t+s)−s=13−14=112

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get P(X≤13|X>14)=1−e−λt=1−e−(3)⋅(1/12)=1−e−1/4

q-253929.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(2),$ calculate $P(X>6\,|\,X>4).$
q-253929.worked_solution:
Given a random variable $X∼Exp(\lambda ),$ and two positive real numbers $s,t,$ the momeryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =2,$ $s=4,$ and $s+t=6.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=6-4=2
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>6\,|\,X>4) & ={e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & ={e}^{-(2)\cdot (2)} \\  & ={e}^{-4} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$
